content.value_statement: React teams need secure authentication flows that handle sessions, redirects, OAuth, and token refresh correctly. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical patterns for building those flows in web apps.
actual_capabilities: Compares token storage options, including httpOnly cookies, localStorage, and memory state.
Shows a cookie-based API client pattern for login, logout, and current user checks.
Provides a React auth context with loading state, login, logout, refresh, and guard helpers.
Covers Google OAuth and NextAuth.js provider configuration examples.
Demonstrates protected routes for React Router and Next.js App Router.
Includes examples for token refresh, login form validation, CSRF headers, and FastAPI endpoints.
limitations: The examples are templates and require adaptation to each backend and identity provider.
The skill does not verify production cookie, CORS, or TLS settings automatically.
It does not provide a complete password storage or user database implementation.
OAuth provider setup still requires external console configuration and secret management.

use_cases.description: Create a login flow with cookie-backed sessions, current user loading, and logout behavior.

use_cases.title: Configure OAuth In Next.js
use_cases.description: Set up Google OAuth or NextAuth.js with provider callbacks and session access in components.

use_cases.title: Harden Authentication UX
use_cases.description: Add protected routes, token refresh, form validation, CSRF headers, and security response headers.

prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate implementation with a backend session API.

prompt_templates.title: Add OAuth To Next.js
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the web-auth skill to add Google OAuth to a Next.js app with NextAuth.js, callbacks, and protected dashboard pages.

output_examples.input: I need login and logout in a React app using cookies.
output_examples.output: A concise implementation plan with an API client, auth provider, loading state, login form connection, and logout cleanup.

output_examples.input: I want to add Google sign-in to a Next.js app.
output_examples.output: Provider setup guidance, environment variable names, callback behavior, session handling, and dashboard protection steps.

output_examples.input: Check my authentication flow for common security gaps.
output_examples.output: A prioritized review covering token storage, CSRF headers, cookie settings, refresh retries, route guards, and error handling.

best_practices: Prefer httpOnly secure cookies for long-lived session tokens when the backend supports them.
Pair cookie authentication with CSRF protection and explicit credential handling in requests.
Protect routes on both the client and server when the framework supports server checks.
anti_patterns: Do not store long-lived access tokens in localStorage without accepting the XSS exposure.
Do not trust a client route guard as the only authorization control.
Do not expose OAuth client secrets in browser code or public environment variables.

faq.question: Does this skill implement a complete auth service?
faq.answer: No. It provides patterns and examples that you adapt to your backend, database, and identity provider.

faq.question: Which React frameworks does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers plain React patterns, React Router, Next.js App Router, and NextAuth.js examples.

faq.question: Does it recommend localStorage for tokens?
faq.answer: It lists localStorage as an option but clearly marks it as unsafe against XSS.

faq.question: Can Claude Code or Codex use this for implementation?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples are structured so Claude Code and Codex can adapt them into project files.

faq.question: Does it handle backend authentication?
faq.answer: It includes a FastAPI reference example, but backend validation and persistence remain project-specific.

faq.question: What should I configure before production?
faq.answer: Review cookie flags, TLS, CORS, CSRF protection, OAuth redirects, secret storage, and server-side authorization.
